newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. data weighs on German shares in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. data weighs on German shares in bourse trade.

text.p: German shares fell sharply in early bourse trade on Friday as Wall Street took a hammering overnight amid fears of a U.S. interest rate hike and the dollar continued its recent weak run

The Dow Jones index of U.S. blue-chips closed over one percent lower, and the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips, took its cue from Wall Street to stand at 18.45 points, or 0.72 percent, at 2,541.61 points.
With little corporate news due on Friday, and a holiday in the U.S. on Monday next, dealers were pessimistic about any new direction for the market until Tuesday.
U.S. GDP data for the second quarter showed a 4.8 percent increase, prompting fears of the first U.S. interest rate increase since February 1995.

One trader said that Daimler Benz AG, which reported a massive improvement in first half profitability on Thursday, would trade lower over the day as there were no further expectations to drive the share higher.
Shares in Daimler were down 92 pfennigs at 80.38 marks in early bourse trade.
Engineering group Mannesmann AG was up 3.30 marks at 534.80 marks in bourse trade, after unconfirmed market rumours that the share had been upgraded by analysts.
